shortcut_name: assume one camp is a maximum independent set
evidence: "# 1. bipartition", "left_nodes = []", "right_nodes = []"; the other solutions likewise begin by finding camps and select a camp rather than considering mixed-camp groups
affordance_in_statement: In this network the users split into two camps, and every friendship connects a user in one camp to a user in the other — there are no friendships between two users of the same camp.
removal_suggestion: Keep the bipartite guarantee, but explicitly state that a valid all-strangers group may contain users from both camps and may exist even when neither individual camp has k users; describe the task as finding an independent set, not choosing a camp.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Bipartitions the graph and treats one entire camp, typically the larger one, as the candidate maximum all-strangers group.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: In this network the users split into two camps, and every friendship connects a user in one camp to a user in the other — there are no friendships between two users of the same camp.

common_affordance: The assumption that an answer can be obtained by selecting users from a single bipartition camp, without solving for a potentially larger independent set that mixes the camps.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It bipartitions the graph and relies on camp membership as the solution criterion, overlooking independent sets containing vertices from both camps.
Its special handling of m = 0 is correct, but its general bipartition-based strategy assumes camp size determines feasibility and misses mixed-camp independent sets.
It similarly starts by finding the two camps and uses the camps as candidate all-strangers groups instead of computing the maximum independent set in the bipartite graph.

recommended_edit: Add an explicit clarification immediately after the camp guarantee: "Do not assume that a valid group lies within one camp. A required group may use users from both camps, and it can exist even when neither camp alone contains k users."
regression_risk: This clarification could cause the already-defeated camp-selection implementations to be corrected and become solving if their authors revise them to use bipartite matching.
